```{r}
str(df)
```

```{r}
total_sample = nrow(df)
category_ratio <- category_counts / total_sample
genre_ratio <- genre_counts / total_sample
tag_ratio <- tag_counts / total_sample
```

To avoid too specific types, we set threshold 1% for categories and genres and 5% for tags. We chose higher threshold for tags as it is more diverse but skewed to certain tags making the dataset too sparse and unique.
```{r}
threshold <- 0.01
threshold_tag <- 0.05

selected_categories <- names(category_ratio[category_ratio >= threshold])
selected_genres <- names(genre_ratio[genre_ratio >= threshold])
selected_tags <- names(tag_ratio[tag_ratio >= threshold_tag])
```

```{r}
length(selected_categories)
length(selected_genres)
length(selected_tags)
```

Check if there is duplicates
e.g. Action in categories and Action in tags
```{r}
common1 <- unique(intersect(selected_categories, selected_genres))
common2 <- unique(intersect(selected_categories, selected_tags))
common3 <- unique(intersect(selected_tags, selected_genres))

length(common1)
length(common2)
length(common3)
```
There is duplicate that can cause multicolinearity between genres and tags.

```{r}
common3
```

Remove those in tags
```{r}
duplicate_tags <- c(
  "Indie", "Action", "Casual",
  "Adventure", "Simulation", "Strategy",
  "RPG", "Early Access"
)

selected_tags <- setdiff(selected_tags, duplicate_tags)
```

Make each selected types in features as features
```{r}
selected_features <- make.names(
  c(
    paste0("Category_", selected_categories),
    paste0("Genre_", selected_genres),
    paste0("Tag_", selected_tags)
  )
)

df[selected_features] <- 0L
```

```{r}
# ChatGPT for filling function
fill_features <- function(df, column, selected, prefix) {

  values <- df[[column]]
  values[is.na(values)] <- ""

  split_values <- strsplit(values, ",")
  split_values <- lapply(split_values, trimws)

  for (feature in selected) {

    feature_name <- make.names(paste0(prefix, "_", feature))

    df[[feature_name]] <- as.integer(
      sapply(split_values, function(x) {
        feature %in% x
      })
    )
  }

  return(df)
}


df <- fill_features(
  df, "Categories", selected_categories, "Category"
)

df <- fill_features(
  df, "Genres", selected_genres, "Genre"
)

df <- fill_features(
  df, "Tags", selected_tags, "Tag"
)
```

Remove categories, genres, tags as they are now used with one hot encoding
```{r}
df$Categories <- NULL
df$Genres <- NULL
df$Tags <- NULL
```
